capabilities: Draw all open tasks as a turnable radial wheel with domains as wedges and hierarchy as rings
Review tasks one stop at a time through a fixed reading wedge and card
Edit tasks (tick, defer, reprioritise, rename, move, add subtasks) writing straight back to the source note
Filter rounds by words, status, date, priority, tag, or heading
Carry tasks or whole headings to other notes, preserving their heading path
disambiguation: Not a task manager or capture tool; it visualises and reviews checkboxes already written in your notes and writes edits back to them.
extras: Free and GPL-3.0, fully local with no network calls, telemetry, or account; installable via BRAT; manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author built it because a list of thousands of checkboxes is not reviewable — you lose your place and never know whether you reached the end.
problem: Long task lists are hard to review completely: you scroll, lose your place, and can never be sure you have seen every open task.

relations.evidence: ticking a task off goes through it, so recurring tasks roll over exactly as Tasks itself would do it

summary: Radial task wheel that draws every open checkbox in the vault as a turnable wheel, so you can review all open tasks one stop at a time.
